correctAnswer: The user's phone is set to the wrong time

questionBank.stem: After entering a password, a user receives a text message containing a one-time verification code. Which delivery method is being used for the second MFA prompt?
questionBank.explanation: A code sent by text message is SMS-based MFA.

questionBank.stem: In voice call multifactor authentication, a user receives a one-time verification code or approval prompt through an automated or live telephone call.
questionBank.explanation: True. Voice call MFA delivers the code or approval prompt by phone call.

questionBank.stem: Which of the following statements about TOTP is not true?
questionBank.explanation: TOTP codes are only valid for a short, recurring time window (for example 30 seconds), so this statement is false.
options: Generated offline using a shared secret and the current time
Requires time synchronization between client and server
Its validity does not depend on short, recurring time intervals
Commonly implemented in authenticator apps and hardware tokens
correctAnswer: Its validity does not depend on short, recurring time intervals

questionBank.stem: Which acronym is used to describe a general category of single-use authentication codes?
questionBank.explanation: A one-time password/passcode (OTP) is a single-use code. TOTP is one type of OTP.

questionBank.stem: Which of the following is a markup language used for exchanging authentication and authorization data?
questionBank.explanation: SAML (Security Assertion Markup Language) is an XML-based format for exchanging authentication and authorization data, and is often used for SSO.

questionBank.stem: An authentication subsystem that enables a user to access multiple, connected system components (such as separate hosts on a network) after a single login on only one of the components is called:
questionBank.explanation: Single sign-on (SSO) lets one login give access to multiple connected systems.

questionBank.stem: Which of the answers listed below refers to a security measure that grants temporary, on-demand, and limited-time access to privileged accounts?
questionBank.explanation: Just-in-time (JIT) access gives privileged access only when it is needed, and only for a limited time.

questionBank.stem: Which of the following refers to a cybersecurity tool dedicated to managing, monitoring, and securing access to critical systems and accounts with elevated privileges?
questionBank.explanation: Privileged access management (PAM) manages, monitors and secures privileged accounts.

questionBank.stem: Which type of software provides a solution specifically designed to centrally manage, monitor, and secure mobile devices such as smartphones and tablets?
questionBank.explanation: Mobile device management (MDM) centrally manages and secures smartphones and tablets.

questionBank.stem: Which of the acronyms listed below refers to a dedicated software or hardware-based security solution designed to detect and prevent unauthorized use and transmission of confidential information?
questionBank.explanation: Data loss prevention (DLP) detects and blocks unauthorized use or transmission of confidential data.

questionBank.stem: Which of the following refers to a comprehensive security framework that manages the entire lifecycle of a digital identity (such as a user account or device) and controls how it can access organizational resources?
questionBank.explanation: Identity and access management (IAM) manages the lifecycle of identities and their access to resources.

questionBank.stem: Which of the statements listed below apply to Windows domains? (Select 3 answers)
questionBank.explanation: A domain is client-server. Accounts and security policies are administered centrally, and one set of credentials works on any domain computer.
options: Each computer on a Windows domain is governed by its own security policy
Logging into any computer on a Windows domain requires a single set of credentials
Windows domains are based on P2P networking architecture
Security policies and permissions on a Windows domain are administered centrally
All members of a Windows domain must be on the same local network or subnet
Windows domains are based on client-server networking architecture
correctAnswer: Logging into any computer on a Windows domain requires a single set of credentials
Security policies and permissions on a Windows domain are administered centrally
Windows domains are based on client-server networking architecture

questionBank.stem: Which of the following answers apply to Windows workgroups? (Select 3 answers)
questionBank.explanation: A workgroup is peer-to-peer. Every computer has its own accounts and its own security policy, and it suits small networks of fewer than about twenty computers.
options: Security policies and permissions in workgroups are administered centrally
Logging into any computer on a workgroup requires a single account (single sign-on feature)
Workgroups are typically recommended for small networks of fewer than twenty computers
There is no limit on the number of hosts that can become a part of a single workgroup
Logging into any computer in a workgroup requires an account on that computer
Each computer in a workgroup has its own security policy
correctAnswer: Workgroups are typically recommended for small networks of fewer than twenty computers
Logging into any computer in a workgroup requires an account on that computer
Each computer in a workgroup has its own security policy

questionBank.stem: Which of the statements listed below are true? (Select 3 answers)
questionBank.explanation: Every Windows computer on a network belongs to either a workgroup or a domain. Workplace networks usually use domains and home networks usually use workgroups.
options: Windows-based computers on home networks must be part of a HomeGroup
Windows-based computers on a network must be part of a workgroup or a domain
Windows-based computers on workplace networks are usually part of a domain
Windows-based computers on workplace networks are usually part of a workgroup
Windows-based computers on home networks are usually part of a workgroup
Windows-based computers on home networks are usually part of a domain
correctAnswer: Windows-based computers on a network must be part of a workgroup or a domain
Windows-based computers on workplace networks are usually part of a domain
Windows-based computers on home networks are usually part of a workgroup

questionBank.stem: Which of the following tools, available in the premium editions of Microsoft Windows, enables administrative control of desktop and user interface settings for all users on a device?
questionBank.explanation: The Group Policy Editor (gpedit.msc) is available in Pro, Enterprise and similar editions. It controls desktop and UI settings centrally.

questionBank.stem: Which Microsoft-proprietary protocol enables remote access and administration of another networked host through a graphical user interface?
questionBank.explanation: Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) is Microsoft's proprietary protocol for graphical remote access (port 3389).

questionBank.stem: Most client editions of 32-bit Microsoft Windows are limited to 4 GB of usable RAM, regardless of the version or edition.
questionBank.explanation: True. 32-bit Windows can address only about 4 GB of RAM.

questionBank.stem: What is the name of a Microsoft Windows feature that enables encryption of entire drives?
questionBank.explanation: BitLocker is the Windows full-drive encryption feature. FileVault is the macOS equivalent.

questionBank.stem: A Microsoft Windows MMC snap-in that allows local administrators to manage system and user configuration policies is called:
questionBank.explanation: gpedit.msc is the Local Group Policy Editor. gpmc.msc is the domain Group Policy Management Console.

questionBank.stem: A Trojan horse is a type of software that performs harmful actions under the guise of a legitimate and useful program. The most characteristic feature of a Trojan horse is that while it may function as a legitimate program and offer expected functionality, it also contains a concealed portion of malicious code that the user is unaware of.
questionBank.explanation: True. A Trojan looks legitimate and works normally but hides malicious code.

questionBank.stem: Which of the answers listed below refers to a collection of software tools used by a hacker to mask intrusion and obtain administrator-level access on a computer or network?
questionBank.explanation: A rootkit hides the intrusion and gives the attacker administrator-level access.

questionBank.stem: Which of the following statements apply to the definition of a computer virus? (Select 2 answers)
questionBank.explanation: A virus is self-replicating code that attaches to a host application or executable. A standalone program that spreads over a network is a worm.
options: A self-replicating computer program that contains a malicious segment
Malicious code that typically attaches itself to an application or executable component
A standalone malicious program that replicates itself over a network
Malware that can operate independently without any interaction
A self-contained malicious program that does not require a host to propagate
correctAnswer: A self-replicating computer program that contains a malicious segment
Malicious code that typically attaches itself to an application or executable component

questionBank.stem: Malicious software collecting information about users without their knowledge/consent is referred to as:
questionBank.explanation: Spyware secretly collects information about the user without consent.

questionBank.stem: Malware that restricts access to a computer system by encrypting files or locking the entire system until the user performs a requested action is known as:
questionBank.explanation: Ransomware locks or encrypts files and demands a payment or action to restore access.

questionBank.stem: Which of the answers listed below refer to examples of spyware? (Select 2 answers)
questionBank.explanation: Stalkerware and keyloggers are spyware that monitor the user. A backdoor and a rootkit are different malware types.

questionBank.stem: A type of malware that infects the storage drive area containing the necessary data and code used to start the OS is called:
questionBank.explanation: A boot sector virus infects the area of the drive that holds the startup code for the OS.

questionBank.stem: Which of the following answers refers to a malware type designed to exploit computing resources without the owner's consent?
questionBank.explanation: A cryptominer uses the victim's CPU/GPU resources to mine cryptocurrency without consent.

questionBank.stem: Which of the answers listed below describes the key characteristics of stalkerware? (Select best answer)
questionBank.explanation: Stalkerware covertly monitors a person's location, calls, messages and app usage, usually on a phone.
options: Provides hidden remote access while transmitting user activity to an external party
Captures on-screen output and periodic screenshots to reveal user activity
Installs tracking cookies and monitors user activity across websites for profiling
Collects location data, call logs, messages, and app usage for continuous monitoring
correctAnswer: Collects location data, call logs, messages, and app usage for continuous monitoring

questionBank.stem: Fileless malware: (Select 3 answers)
questionBank.explanation: Fileless malware runs in memory, abuses legitimate OS tools, and evades signature-based antivirus because it writes no payload file.
options: Modifies the boot sector of the storage drive for persistence
Requires a rootkit to hide its presence on a drive
Abuses legitimate operating system tools to execute code
Operates entirely in RAM without writing its payload to storage
correctAnswer: Abuses legitimate operating system tools to execute code
Operates entirely in RAM without writing its payload to storage

questionBank.stem: A user reports slow system performance and suspicious pop-ups, and a technician confirms a malware infection. Which action should the technician perform immediately after investigating and verifying the malware symptoms?
questionBank.explanation: The order is: investigate and verify, then quarantine the infected system so the malware can't spread.

questionBank.stem: After confirming a malware infection on a Windows Home PC, which action related to System Restore should be performed before beginning remediation?
questionBank.explanation: Disable System Restore before remediation, because old restore points may contain the malware.
options: Delete user data but keep restore points intact
Create a new system restore point immediately before removal
Disable System Restore to prevent reinfection from infected restore points
Leave System Restore enabled to preserve recovery options
correctAnswer: Disable System Restore to prevent reinfection from infected restore points

questionBank.stem: A technician suspects a Windows 11 host is infected with persistent malware that prevents standard removal tools from running effectively. Which solution provides a minimal Windows environment that enables malware scanning and removal with reduced risk of interference?
questionBank.explanation: Safe Mode loads a minimal set of drivers and services, so malware is less likely to interfere with scanning and removal.

questionBank.stem: Windows Preinstallation Environment (WinPE) is a lightweight version of Windows that can be booted from removable media. When used for malware removal, WinPE runs entirely outside the installed operating system, providing a minimal, trusted environment for offline scanning and remediation. Because it does not load the host OS's services, drivers, or resident processes, the ability of in-OS malware to execute or interfere with removal is greatly reduced. This isolation makes WinPE especially effective for addressing persistent infections that can evade standard removal tools while Windows is running.
questionBank.explanation: True. WinPE booted from removable media runs outside the infected OS, so resident malware can't interfere.

questionBank.stem: Which scenario best justifies performing a full OS reinstall or system reimage?
questionBank.explanation: Reimaging or reinstalling is the last resort when malware survives repeated scanning and removal.
options: Failed major OS upgrades or feature updates

questionBank.stem: Which of the steps listed below are part of the remediation phase in the malware removal process? (Select 3 answers)
questionBank.explanation: Remediation covers updating the anti-malware software, scanning and removal, and reimaging/reinstalling if needed. Quarantine and disabling System Restore happen earlier.

questionBank.stem: After successfully removing malware from a client's Windows PC, which step should a technician perform next to maintain ongoing system protection?
questionBank.explanation: After remediation, schedule scans and run updates. Then enable System Restore and create a restore point, and finally educate the user.

questionBank.stem: In the malware removal process on the Windows Home PC, the primary security reason for delaying the enabling of System Restore until after all security updates have been applied is to ensure the new restore point is completely clean and patched against known vulnerabilities.
questionBank.explanation: True. System Restore is re-enabled and a restore point created only after the system is clean and fully updated.

questionBank.stem: According to CompTIA's best practice procedures for malware removal, the last step of the malware removal process should be:
questionBank.explanation: In CompTIA's SOHO malware removal list, educating the end user is the final step (step 10).
options: Documenting findings, actions, outcomes, and conclusions

questionBank.stem: Which of the answers listed below refers to Windows command-line command used for directory traversal?
questionBank.explanation: cd (change directory) moves between directories. dir only lists contents.

questionBank.stem: Which of the following Windows command-line commands can be used to list all files and subdirectories in the current directory?
questionBank.explanation: dir lists the files and subdirectories in the current directory. dir /? shows help.

questionBank.stem: What is the name of a Windows command-line utility that can be used to display TCP/IP configuration settings?
questionBank.explanation: ipconfig displays TCP/IP configuration. ifconfig is the Linux tool.

questionBank.stem: A Windows command-line utility used for checking the reachability of a remote network host is called:
questionBank.explanation: ping tests whether a remote host is reachable.

questionBank.stem: The netstat command-line utility is used for: (Select 2 answers)
questionBank.explanation: netstat displays active connections and listening ports, and network protocol statistics.
options: Testing the reachability of a remote host
Displaying intermediary points on the packet route

questionBank.stem: Which of the network command-line tools listed below resolves a domain name to an IP address?
questionBank.explanation: nslookup queries DNS to resolve a domain name to an IP address.

questionBank.stem: Which of the Windows command-line commands is used to manage connections to network resources?
questionBank.explanation: net use connects to and disconnects from shared network resources, including mapping drive letters.

questionBank.stem: A network command-line utility in Windows that tracks and displays the route taken by IP packets on their way to another host is known as:
questionBank.explanation: tracert is the Windows route-tracing tool. traceroute is its Linux counterpart.

questionBank.stem: Which network command-line utility in Windows combines the features of ping and traceroute?
questionBank.explanation: pathping combines ping and tracert, tracing the route and measuring latency and packet loss at each hop.

questionBank.stem: Which of the following command-line utilities in Windows is used to verify file system integrity and fix logical file system errors?
questionBank.explanation: chkdsk checks the file system and disk for errors and can repair them.

questionBank.stem: Which command-line tool in Windows initializes a drive by setting it up with a structure that supports file storage?
questionBank.explanation: format prepares a drive with a file system structure for file storage.

questionBank.stem: Which of the commands in Windows launches a text-based, command-line partitioning utility?
questionBank.explanation: diskpart is the text-based, command-line partitioning utility in Windows.

questionBank.stem: Which of the answers listed below refers to a Windows command-line command used to create a directory or subdirectory?
questionBank.explanation: md (or mkdir) creates a directory.

questionBank.stem: Which of the following command-line commands in Windows can be used to delete a directory?
questionBank.explanation: rmdir (or rd) removes a directory. del deletes files.

questionBank.stem: Which copying utility accessible via Windows command line interface offers the widest range of options?
questionBank.explanation: robocopy (Robust File Copy) has the widest range of options, including retries, mirroring and resume.

questionBank.stem: Which command-line command in Windows displays the name of the current computer a user is connected to?
questionBank.explanation: hostname displays the name of the current computer.

questionBank.stem: Which of the Windows command-line commands, when run on a Windows computer without additional parameters, lists all local user accounts configured on that specific computer?
questionBank.explanation: net user with no parameters lists the local user accounts on the computer.

questionBank.stem: Which of the command-line commands in Windows launches a pop-up window containing a brief summary of the installed operating system?
questionBank.explanation: winver opens a small pop-up window showing the Windows version and build. msinfo32 opens the larger System Information tool.

questionBank.stem: Which command-line utility provides information about the currently logged-on Windows user?
questionBank.explanation: whoami displays the currently logged-on user. id and logname are Linux commands.

questionBank.stem: What is the standard syntax in Windows command line for displaying help or usage information related to a specific utility?
questionBank.explanation: Appending /? to a command shows its help and usage.

questionBank.stem: A Windows command-line utility that refreshes Group Policy settings on a local computer without requiring a restart or logoff is called:
questionBank.explanation: gpupdate refreshes Group Policy settings without a restart or logoff.

questionBank.stem: Which of the answers listed below refers to a command-line tool in Windows that can be used to display current Group Policy settings for a user or computer?
questionBank.explanation: gpresult displays the Group Policy settings applied to a user or computer.

questionBank.stem: The sfc command-line utility in Windows: (Select 2 answers)
questionBank.explanation: System File Checker (sfc) scans the integrity of protected system files and replaces incorrect versions with the correct Microsoft versions. Checking disk volumes is chkdsk.
options: Scans disk volumes for file system errors
Identifies and recovers readable data from bad sectors on a drive
Encrypts files to prevent unauthorized access to sensitive data
Replaces incorrect system file versions with correct Microsoft versions
Scans the integrity of all protected system files
correctAnswer: Replaces incorrect system file versions with correct Microsoft versions
Scans the integrity of all protected system files

questionBank.stem: Which command-line command in MS Windows moves the command-line prompt one folder up in the directory tree (sets the prompt at the parent folder of the current folder)?
questionBank.explanation: cd .. moves up one level to the parent folder.

questionBank.stem: Which of the following Windows command-line commands changes the current directory to the root directory?
questionBank.explanation: cd \ changes to the root directory of the current drive.

questionBank.stem: A Windows technician needs to locate all .exe files within a directory, including those in its subdirectories. Which command should they use?
questionBank.explanation: The /s switch makes dir search the current directory and all its subdirectories.

questionBank.stem: Which of the answers listed below refers to an ipconfig parameter used for displaying the full TCP/IP configuration information for all adapters?
questionBank.explanation: ipconfig /all shows the full TCP/IP configuration for all adapters.

questionBank.stem: Which command-line commands in MS Windows are used to refresh the DHCP configuration for all network adapters? (Select 2 answers)
questionBank.explanation: ipconfig /release drops the current DHCP lease and ipconfig /renew requests a new one.

questionBank.stem: A user reports an inability to access any websites or network shares. As the first troubleshooting step, a technician needs to verify whether the TCP/IP stack on the local Windows machine is functioning correctly. Which ping command should they use for this initial test?
questionBank.explanation: 127.0.0.1 is the loopback address, so pinging it tests the local TCP/IP stack without involving the network.

questionBank.stem: Which netstat parameter is used to display all active TCP/UDP connections and listening ports?
questionBank.explanation: netstat -a displays all connections and listening ports.

questionBank.stem: The -b netstat parameter in Microsoft Windows allows users to view the name of the application associated with each active connection or listening port.
questionBank.explanation: True. netstat -b shows the executable that created each connection or listening port (it needs elevation).

questionBank.stem: Which parameter, when used with the netstat command, displays addresses and port numbers in numerical form?
questionBank.explanation: netstat -n shows addresses and port numbers in numerical form without resolving names.

questionBank.stem: Which of the command-line tools listed below can be used for troubleshooting DNS-related problems?
questionBank.explanation: nslookup queries DNS servers and is the Windows tool for DNS troubleshooting.

questionBank.stem: A technician needs to map a network share located at \\SERVER\Data to the drive letter Z: on a user's computer. Which of the following commands should the technician use?
questionBank.explanation: The syntax is net use Z: \\SERVER\Data (drive letter first, then the UNC path).

questionBank.stem: The output of the Windows tracert command-line utility primarily displays a list of all intermediate routers (hops) that an IP packet traverses to reach a specified destination, along with the round-trip time (latency) to each of those hops. This information is useful for identifying network bottlenecks, diagnosing where delays or packet loss are occurring, and determining whether a routing issue is within the local network, the ISP, or further along the internet path.
questionBank.explanation: True. tracert lists each hop and its round-trip time, which helps locate where delays occur.

questionBank.stem: What are the most important functionalities provided by the pathping utility? (Select 2 answers)
questionBank.explanation: pathping traces the path to the destination and measures latency and packet loss at each hop.
options: Tests connectivity to a specific port
Traces the path to the destination
Sends broadcast messages over the network
correctAnswer: Traces the path to the destination

questionBank.stem: The /f switch of the chkdsk command-line utility in MS Windows instructs the utility to:
questionBank.explanation: chkdsk /f fixes file system errors. /r also locates bad sectors and recovers readable data.
options: Scan the system for corrupted or missing system files
Automatically repair detected file system errors on the disk
Identify bad sectors on the disk and attempt to recover any readable data from them
Optimize disk usage by consolidating fragmented file data
correctAnswer: Automatically repair detected file system errors on the disk

questionBank.stem: The chkdsk /r command in Windows: (Select 2 answers)
questionBank.explanation: chkdsk /r identifies bad sectors and attempts to recover readable data from them. Repairing system files is sfc, and defragmenting is a separate tool.
options: Compresses files on the disk to save space
Attempts to recover any readable data from bad sectors
Optimizes disk usage by consolidating fragmented file data
Scans for and repairs corrupted system files
Identifies bad sectors on the disk
correctAnswer: Attempts to recover any readable data from bad sectors
Identifies bad sectors on the disk

questionBank.stem: A technician is preparing to reinstall Windows on a user's PC. They want to quickly prepare the D: drive by removing all file system references to existing data without performing a thorough overwrite. Which variant of the format command in the Windows command-line interface should they use to achieve that goal?
questionBank.explanation: format /q performs a quick format. It removes file system references without overwriting the data.

questionBank.stem: A user is trying to clean and repartition a disk with the diskpart command-line utility in Windows, but encounters an "Access is denied" error. What is the most likely cause of this problem?
questionBank.explanation: diskpart needs an elevated prompt (Run as administrator). Without it you get "Access is denied".
options: The drive is offline and needs to be brought online first
The utility is trying to access a non-existent drive
The drive is currently in use by another application and is locked
The utility was not launched with administrative privileges
correctAnswer: The utility was not launched with administrative privileges

questionBank.stem: What is the difference between md and mkdir command-line commands in MS Windows?
questionBank.explanation: md is simply the short form of mkdir. Both do the same thing.
options: The md command supports creating multiple directories at once, while mkdir does not
The mkdir command requires administrative privileges, while md does not
The md command is specific to older MS DOS versions, mkdir is for modern Windows
There is no difference, as both commands provide the same functionality
correctAnswer: There is no difference, as both commands provide the same functionality

questionBank.stem: A user wants to delete the entire directory named Data located at C:\Files\Data along with all its subdirectories and files using the Windows command-line. Which variant of the rmdir command should they run?
questionBank.explanation: The correct command would be rmdir C:\Files\Data /s. All of the listed options point at C:\Files, which would target the wrong directory.

questionBank.stem: A Windows technician is setting up an automated nightly task to copy an entire folder tree, including all subdirectories and empty folders, from a network drive to a local backup location. The process must retry failed copies automatically. Which command-line utility should they use?
questionBank.explanation: robocopy supports copying whole trees including empty folders and automatically retrying failed copies.

questionBank.stem: A user needs to copy a very large volume of files from one Windows host to another. The task must resume automatically if interrupted due to network issues. Which command-line tool is best suited for this task?
questionBank.explanation: robocopy can resume interrupted copies and retry on failure, which suits large network transfers.

questionBank.stem: A technician suspects that a Windows user account named guest has been locked out or disabled due to multiple failed login attempts. The technician also needs to check when the account last logged in and whether it requires a password. Which of the following commands will provide this information?
questionBank.explanation: net user guest shows account details such as status, last logon and whether a password is required.

questionBank.stem: A support technician is remotely connected to multiple Windows machines and needs to confirm the network identity of the computer they are currently operating on. Which command should they use to verify this?
questionBank.explanation: hostname displays the computer's name.

questionBank.stem: An IT technician needs to confirm the Windows OS version and build number to verify its compatibility with an upcoming system patch. Which command-line command should they run?
questionBank.explanation: winver shows the Windows version and build number.

questionBank.stem: A Windows technician wants to view a comprehensive snapshot of the current user's security context, including its privileges, group memberships, logon ID, and security identifiers. Which whoami parameter should they use?
questionBank.explanation: whoami /all displays the user, groups, privileges, logon ID and SIDs together.

questionBank.stem: In the Windows command line environment, which common syntax can be used as an alternative to appending /? after a command name to display help?
questionBank.explanation: help [command name] displays help for that command, the same as [command name] /?.

questionBank.stem: Used without any parameters, the help command in MS Windows displays a list of available system commands along with a brief description of each command.
questionBank.explanation: True. help with no parameters lists the available commands with short descriptions.

questionBank.stem: What is the default behavior of the gpupdate command-line command in Windows if no parameters are specified?
questionBank.explanation: With no parameters, gpupdate refreshes both user and computer policies. /target limits it to one.
options: It does not refresh any policies
It refreshes both user and computer policies
correctAnswer: It refreshes both user and computer policies

questionBank.stem: During a routine audit, an IT technician needs a concise report of all Group Policy settings that have been applied to a specific host. Which gpresult parameter in Windows command line instructs the utility to provide this summary?
questionBank.explanation: gpresult /r displays a summary of the Group Policy results. /s specifies a remote computer.

questionBank.stem: Which parameter of the sfc command in Windows command line enables a file check that scans integrity of all protected system files and attempts to repair corrupted files?
questionBank.explanation: sfc /scannow scans all protected system files and repairs corrupted ones.

questionBank.stem: Windows 10 and Windows 11 N editions are special regional versions of Microsoft Windows designed for the European market. They are identical to their standard counterparts in terms of core functionality but exclude certain preinstalled multimedia features. The "N" designation refers specifically to the absence of Windows Media Player and related multimedia components in these editions.
questionBank.explanation: True. N editions leave out Windows Media Player and related multimedia components.

questionBank.stem: The Home editions for Windows 10 and Windows 11 support participation in workgroups, but do not support joining Active Directory domains.
questionBank.explanation: True. Home editions can't join an Active Directory domain. Pro and higher can.

questionBank.stem: Premium editions of Microsoft Windows 10 and 11 allow IT administrators to customize, restrict, or lock down specific user interface elements, such as disabling access to certain settings, hiding specific Start Menu items, or enforcing standardized desktop backgrounds. This is in contrast to Windows 10 and 11 Home editions, which offer only basic personalization features in that respect.
questionBank.explanation: True. Group Policy in the premium editions allows that kind of lockdown, and Home doesn't have it.
